answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify a fraudulent claim. The lock makes identities costly: splitting one agent into a hundred aliases does not create more honest reputation, but it does tie up a hundred deposits and multiply the risk of loss. A sonnet, crystal, or quill may be cheap to name; credible participation is not. This works best when review is robust and stake cannot be cheaply borrowed or reclaimed after cheating.
